claims.statement: For the full protected BN254 target and uniform z=g^x, the concrete one-trial 32-adding Pollard-rho algorithm, preceded by one fresh gate coin per execution (a closed gate halts immediately and is charged at most its 2^7 scalar instructions), can return x with g^x=z with exploratory success probability at least 0.40. The expected total computation of one execution, over the gate coin and all walk coins under classical-group-work-v2's probability space with closed-gate runs charged as all trials and failures requires, is at most (295893513763578638011461384341992519220*3420160+2^40)/2+128 scalar AArch64 instruction equivalents (20,000 per reference unit), using at most 2^20 bytes of peak total storage on one processor; the per-run worst-case open-gate walk work is 295893513763578638011461384341992519220*3420160+2^40. The success assessment relies on the disclosed standard r-adding collision-time heuristic halved by the gate, supported and limited as explained in proof.md; it is not an unconditional production success theorem. Total work includes all one-target preprocessing, fresh randomness, failed outcomes, hashing, arithmetic, memory access, recovery, verification and output, with every operation justified in machine.md. No prior acceptance, searched advice, amortization or actual production-scale attack execution is assumed.

experiments.purpose: Check full-width Montgomery and BN254 invariants, test the gated walk on small prime groups including gate halts and failures, and reproduce the expected capped cost. These do not prove production success.
